abi.interpretation: emptyExport = managed->guest->managed round trip (lock, stack setup, EnterGuest/Exit). importCallback = guest->managed->guest-return per call (spill, native stack switch, UnmanagedCallersOnly thunk, GuestCall handler). nested = callback + managed->guest re-entry (nop_fn) inside the handler; subtract callback for the nested-call cost.

codeSize.note: Host bytes of a guest instruction include any translator stub emitted between it and the next mapped instruction. Guest bytes include embedded rodata (jump/function tables) that follows each function in .text.

coldStart.note: Whole-process wall time including 'dotnet' host start; the child reads the cached artifact, loads the module and performs one export call.

meta.commandLine: dotnet run -c Release --project benchmarks/BlitzCS.BinaryCompiler.Bench -- --out docs/evidence/m21-binary-benchmark.json   (see docs/binary-benchmark.md; the recorded runs additionally used --reuse-n to keep identical iteration counts between the baseline and optimized builds)
meta.method: Per sample, interleaved (order alternates): (a) native ELF32 oracle process pinned with taskset, self-timed (clock_gettime + rdtsc) around the workload with in-process user-space perf_event_open counters; (b) the same machine code translated and run through GuestModule on the pinned .NET thread, timed with Stopwatch and perf_event_open on that thread. Both run w_init(12345) first and must return identical checksums.

translation.note: BinaryBuild.Translate end-to-end (read file + parse + hash + translate + cache write) in-process after JIT warm-up of the first run; the first cold sample includes JIT.

workloads.description: FNV-1a hash over a 64 KB buffer

workloads.name: crc
workloads.description: table CRC32 over a 64 KB buffer

workloads.name: mem
workloads.description: rep movsd copy + repne scasb scan, 64 KB

repeatRunsNote: All runs are reported, none dropped. The machine is a desktop with background applications, so single runs can be perturbed (e.g. baseline matmul 15.4 percent in one run, 8-9 percent in the others).

baselineBeforeOptimization.description: Same benchmark, same machine and ns/iteration counts (--reuse-n), run against the unmodified CodeGen of commit 9cc097a built in a separate git worktree; 5 runs, interleaved with or taken around the optimized runs (fbase* before the final layout work, gbase* alongside the final build).

translatorRobustness.description: 25 real PE32 DLLs/EXEs found on the benchmark machine (Wine builtin and redistributable libraries, 0.1-2 MB) translated with --translate-stress (translation only, nothing executed). No exceptions; diagnostics identical before/after.

optimizations.name: Loop/function alignment preserved
optimizations.hypothesis: The translation is longer than the original (addr32 prefixes), so loops that the compiler aligned fall across 32-byte fetch windows; matmul inner loop 21 bytes at host offset 0x..30.
optimizations.evidence: matmul +8.1..9.2 percent with identical instruction count (cycles x1.08); 15 alternating samples with/without padding: 7.8-9.0 percent vs 2.0-2.3 percent.
optimizations.change: Branch targets preceded by compiler NOP padding (and dead function entries) are re-aligned to 16 bytes (32 for loops that fit a 32-byte window) with multi-byte NOPs; the compiler padding is dropped. Padding is iterated to a fixed point (pads only grow, so branch relaxation converges).

optimizations.name: Inline dispatch + cmp/jae bounds check where flags are provably dead
optimizations.hypothesis: Every ret/indirect branch pays 12 instructions: shared dispatch jump, SSE movd/pminud/movd clamp (flag preserving) and a shared predictor entry.
optimizations.evidence: Unsafe upper bound experiment (not shipped): replacing the SSE clamp by cmp/jae took ind 47.6 to 27.2, calls 39.6 to 25.0, switch 34.0 to 22.5, fib 27.2 to 18.9 percent (single 9-sample runs).
optimizations.change: When no statically known dispatch target (return sites, non-speculative function entries) consumes arithmetic flags, ret/call [mem|reg]/table jmp use cmp+jae; otherwise the exact flag-preserving SSE clamp is kept (existing test FlagsSurviveCallRetAndIndirectJump). Untranslated or out-of-range targets still trap.

optimizations.name: Static return-site prediction
optimizations.hypothesis: Most rets return to a handful of call sites known at translation time; compare-and-branch is cheaper than the table dispatch and predicted per site by the conditional predictor.
optimizations.evidence: single 9-sample run after O2: fib 17.7 to 10.4, calls 27.8 to 4.7 percent.
optimizations.change: ret compares the popped address against up to 4 statically known return sites (direct callers of the functions that can reach the ret, or all indirect-call sites for address-taken functions) and jumps straight to the translated site; any other value falls through to the generic dispatch.

optimizations.name: Argument pushes + call return push share one ESP adjustment
optimizations.hypothesis: push a; call f lowers to two lea esp adjustments.
optimizations.evidence: fib 9.1 to 0.6 percent in a single run (noisy), instruction count x1.26 to x1.22.
optimizations.change: TryMergePushRun absorbs a following direct call.

optimizations.name: Host-offset shadow tables for read-only jump/pointer tables
optimizations.hypothesis: switch dispatch pays the generic 9-instruction translation of a guest VA that is already known statically.
optimizations.evidence: single 9-sample run: switch 19.7 to 10.0 percent, instructions x1.53 to x1.32.
optimizations.change: jmp/call [table+idx*4] with the table in a non-writable section and relocated pointers to translated blocks goes through an in-code table of host offsets after an idx<count check; the generic path is kept for every other index. Layout is iterated to a fixed point so the tables are exact.

knownLimits: Goal <=1 percent overhead is met (within noise, |median| <= 1 percent) for int, fnv, crc, mem (rep movs/scas), lz, x87, sse.

Not met: ind (+15.9 percent: gcc hoists the table load into a register, so call edx has no table to shadow and uses the generic 9-instruction dispatch), switch (+5.6), calls (+4.6), fib (+2.8), matmul (+1.4, sensitive to code alignment).
The remaining call/ret cost is structural: guest call = 3 host instructions instead of 1 and no return-stack-buffer prediction; closing it needs native call/ret on a separate host stack.
ABI transitions are dominated by managed-side synchronization in GuestModule.Invoke (about 110 ns per empty export call, of which an uncontended RWLS read lock pair ~28 ns and Monitor ~19 ns).
Translation time is 1.5-2.5x slower and host code 10-30 percent larger than before these optimizations (alignment fixed-point passes, inlined dispatch, return-site compares).
